title: [Chapitre] III. Réseaux via découpages : notes manuscrites (08/06/1986).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting (Chapter III, 'Réseaux via découpages', 1986): L is a basic tame ('modéré') space, apparently a line or transversal, or a cell of an arrangement built by successive cuttings (découpages). Mod(L) is the Boolean algebra of tame subsets of L. For A in Mod(L), M_A is the induced Boolean algebra. On the previous page, connected components of an object of such a Boolean algebra are defined algebraically, assuming the algebra is finite: they are the minimal nonempty parts of A that are both open and closed in A. The example being worked: A = X_Φ, the tame set attached to a flag Φ, written as a disjoint finite union of 'positions transversales' (cells) T_i. The claim is that the connected components of A are exactly the T_i. Since A is the join of the T_i and T_i ∧ T_j = ∅ for i ≠ j, it suffices to show (a) each T_i is clopen in A and (b) each T_i is connected.

This page proves both points.

(a) It suffices that T_i is closed in A. The finitely many other T_j are then closed too, so the complement of T_i in A is closed and T_i is also open. Closedness means cl(T_i) ∩ A = T_i, with closure taken in the tame sense. This is called 'immediate'. NB: the tame closure of a transversal position T is the associated closed transversal position. This is T itself if T is a point. If T is not closed, one examines points a in ∂T \ T.

(b) For connectedness, note that the tame structure restricts well: (M_L)_T = M_T. So one may regard T as a transversal in its own right and assume T = L. If X is a tame clopen subset of L, then X = X_φ is a union of cells T_i of some cutting. Clopenness forces each nonempty piece to propagate to all of L, i.e. T_i ≠ ∅ implies T_i = L. Hence X = ∅ (I = ∅) or X = L (I ≠ ∅): L is tamely connected.

Purpose: build a purely combinatorial/Boolean-algebraic notion of connected components inside a finite tame Boolean algebra generated by a cutting. The next page uses it for the one-dimensional case: the Boolean algebra generated by mutually tame subsets of a line has as components the points t_k and the open intervals between them. This is a 1-dimensional cell decomposition, the 'découpage' of L.
errors: Part (a) as stated needs more than A being a finite disjoint union of cells. If A contained both an open cell and one of its boundary cells (e.g. ]0,1[ and {1}), the cell T_i would not be closed in A and the components would not be the T_i. The 'C'est immédiat' must therefore rest on the specific hypothesis on A = X_Φ (a flag-type / 'aminci' condition ensuring that no boundary cell of T_i lies in A), which is not made explicit on this page.

The connectedness argument in (b) is very compressed. Passing from 'X clopen and a union of cells' to 'X = ∅ or L' implicitly uses that the cells of any cutting of L are linked through closure/boundary adjacency. That is essentially the tame connectedness of L, which is not proved here.
The appeal to (M_L)_T = M_T to reduce to T = L presupposes that a transversal position is itself a model space of the same type as L. This is plausible in his framework but asserted without argument.

ideas.what: Connected components of a tame set defined Boolean-algebraically as minimal nonempty clopen elements of a finite Boolean algebra of tame subsets
ideas.modern_name: Definable connectedness / components in o-minimal structures; atoms of a finite Boolean algebra of definable sets
ideas.where_published: Tame topology programme only sketched in Esquisse d'un programme (1984), without these details

ideas.what: Connected components of a set decomposed into cells are the cells (under a suitable 'no adjacent cells' hypothesis); cells are connected
ideas.modern_name: Cell decomposition theorem consequences: cells are definably connected, finitely many definable components

ideas.what: Tame closure of a transversal position (cell) is the associated closed position; frontier ∂T \ T consists of lower-dimensional cells
ideas.modern_name: Frontier condition for stratifications / regular cell complexes

deep.surprise_reason: This is a routine verification inside Grothendieck's unpublished development of tame topology via cuttings, treated as finite Boolean algebras of cells. The results (cells are connected; components of a suitable cell union are its cells) are standard in o-minimality and stratification theory. The only mildly interesting feature is the purely Boolean-algebraic definition of components, which is historically notable but not mathematically new.
transcription_corrections: 'pos. tr.' should be read as 'position transversale' throughout.
'OPS T = L' is most likely the abbreviation 'On peut supposer T = L'.
In the second NB, '{+fermée+} [-associée-]' reflects that 'fermée' is written above the word, giving 'position transversale fermée associée'.

'elle est vide [?] sur [?] les T_i non vides' is probably 'elle est vide [ou contient] les T_i' / 'dans les T_i'. The line is garbled in the image and the logic is that X contains each nonempty T_i it meets.
The final line reads 'donc X = ∅ (I = ∅) ou X = L (I ≠ ∅) OK.'
